prerequisites: Basic knowledge of continuous-time and discrete-time linear dynamic systems analysis.
Use of Laplace, Zeta, and Fourier transforms and software tools for dynamic system analysis and simulation.

learning_outcomes.text: The course aims to introduce students to the design of feedback control laws for dynamic systems and illustrate their possible applications. In particular, the main methodologies for the synthesis of linear control systems, both analog and digital, are explored in depth.
At the end of the course, the student will be able to design linear controllers, also with the aid of software tools for the analysis, design, and simulation of control systems.

The educational path aims to provide methodological tools to understand the fundamental principles of automatic control and the effects of feedback on the dynamic characteristics of linear systems or systems linearized after linearization.

The main methodologies for feedback control design, both analog and digital, in the time domain and in transformed domains will be introduced. This knowledge will enable students to understand the main issues connected with the use of different synthesis methods, depending on the required specifications and the characteristics of the processes to be controlled.
The acquired knowledge will enable students to formalize the specifications required of a control system in the time domain and in transformed domains.
Based on these specifications and the characteristics of the process to be controlled, students will be able to make design choices, i.e., to design the control law using different synthesis methods.
Matlab/Simulink software will be used to support controller synthesis and performance verification.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental properties of feedback control systems: specifications of a control system in the time domain.
Reachability and controllability in continuous time and discrete time. Control to an equilibrium state with state feedback. Output regulation with eigenvalue and gain assignment.
Notes on analog realization and digital realization of a control system. Sampled-data system. Output regulator with integral action and state feedback in continuous time and discrete time.
Observability in continuous time and discrete time. State observer. Eigenvalue separation and output feedback control.
Analysis of output feedback systems: steady-state precision and system type, transient response.
Closed-loop analysis with the root locus method. Design of control systems with root locus in continuous time and discrete time. Typical regulator structures. Control of unstable processes.
Frequency domain analysis of continuous-time systems: stability and robustness with the Nyquist criterion. Stability margins.
Sensitivity functions. Relationships between the time domain response, the open-loop harmonic response function, and the sensitivity functions.
Design of control systems in the frequency domain with the loop transfer function method. Compensator networks.
Design of digital controllers by discretization and directly in the discrete-time domain with the model assignment method.
Problems of digital control realization: structuring of the control algorithm, anti-aliasing filtering, considerations on the choice of the sampling period.
PID controllers: performance analysis in the frequency domain and notes on experimental tuning methods.
Advanced control systems: Smith predictor, cascade control, mixed control schemes with feedback and feedforward.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral exam. The written test includes numerical exercises.
